methodology.risk_score_note: The percentage is a prioritization estimate based on potential impact and likelihood observed externally; it is not a CVSS score.
methodology.limitations: No exploitation, authentication bypass, credential testing, form submission, payment, file upload, SQL injection payload, XSS payload, or destructive action was performed against production.

findings.title: Unsupported PHP runtime disclosed by the server
findings.evidence: X-Powered-By: PHP/8.1.34. PHP 8.1 reached end of life on 2025-12-31.
findings.impact: Future and known defects may remain unpatched, increasing the chance of server compromise if the application reaches a vulnerable runtime path.
findings.remediation: Upgrade after compatibility tests to PHP 8.4 or 8.5, patch the framework and extensions, and remove X-Powered-By.

findings.title: Old jQuery and jQuery UI versions in the donation page
findings.status: Affected versions confirmed; vulnerable data flow not proven
findings.evidence: jquery 3.2.1 and jquery-ui 1.12.1 are loaded. Their affected ranges include CVE-2020-11022, CVE-2020-11023, CVE-2021-41182, CVE-2021-41183, CVE-2021-41184, and CVE-2022-31160.
findings.impact: If untrusted content reaches affected HTML or widget APIs, JavaScript may execute in the donor's browser, allowing page manipulation or theft of data available to the session.
findings.remediation: Upgrade jQuery to a supported current release and jQuery UI to at least 1.13.2, test all donation flows, and review DOM sinks before deployment.

findings.title: Weak CSP combined with unverified third-party scripts
findings.evidence: CSP contains only upgrade-insecure-requests. The page loads 19 external resources; 16 have no SRI, including 10 scripts. Some URLs use floating versions such as aos@next, sweetalert2@8, and toastify-js.
findings.impact: A compromised CDN, dependency, or tag-management account could inject code into the donation page and alter content or collect browser-accessible data.
findings.remediation: Self-host or pin immutable versions, add SRI where applicable, reduce third parties, and deploy a nonce/hash CSP through Report-Only before enforcement.

findings.title: Email anti-spoofing policy is monitoring rather than blocking
findings.evidence: DMARC is v=DMARC1; p=none and SPF ends with ~all. DKIM could not be proven externally without the active selector.
findings.impact: Attackers may have a better chance of delivering phishing messages that impersonate the association and target donors or employees.
findings.remediation: Inventory every sender, validate DKIM alignment, monitor reports, then move DMARC gradually to quarantine and reject.

findings.title: Donation page can be embedded by another site (clickjacking)
findings.status: Confirmed with a non-interactive iframe proof
findings.evidence: No X-Frame-Options and no CSP frame-ancestors. The live donation page rendered inside an independent local iframe.
findings.impact: A malicious page can place deceptive layers above the donation interface and trick a visitor into clicking unintended controls.
findings.remediation: Set CSP frame-ancestors 'self' (or 'none' if framing is unnecessary) and X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN for legacy clients.

findings.title: No HSTS policy
findings.evidence: HTTP redirects to HTTPS, but Strict-Transport-Security is absent.
findings.impact: The first visit is not protected by a browser-persisted HTTPS-only policy, leaving a downgrade opportunity on a hostile network.
findings.remediation: After validating all subdomains, deploy HSTS with a staged max-age and then consider includeSubDomains/preload.

findings.title: Additional browser security headers are missing
findings.evidence: X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, COOP, and CORP are absent.
findings.impact: The browser has fewer restrictions against MIME guessing, referrer leakage, unnecessary device features, and cross-origin interaction.
findings.remediation: Add nosniff, a strict referrer policy, a minimal Permissions-Policy, and test COOP/CORP compatibility with payment providers.

findings.title: State-changing cart request uses GET
findings.status: Confirmed implementation pattern; business impact not tested
findings.evidence: The addtocart JavaScript function sends method: get to add-cart-project and includes a token in query data.
findings.impact: Cross-site requests, browser prefetching, logs, or copied URLs may unexpectedly modify a visitor's cart or expose query parameters.
findings.remediation: Use POST with server-side CSRF validation, keep tokens out of URLs, validate amount and project identifiers server-side, and return no-store.

findings.title: HTML insertion sink requires a stored-XSS review
findings.status: Code indicator only; not exploited or confirmed vulnerable
findings.evidence: donatenow() uses $('#donatenowmodal_porjectname').html(projectname). Current values appear server-generated.
findings.impact: If a project name or related value can contain attacker-controlled HTML, script-capable markup could execute for donors.
findings.remediation: Use textContent/jQuery .text() for names, build option elements with DOM APIs, encode data in JSON safely, and add automated XSS tests in staging.

findings.title: Technology and hosting fingerprints are disclosed
findings.evidence: Server responses disclose LiteSpeed, Hostinger, hPanel, and PHP/8.1.34.
findings.impact: This shortens attacker reconnaissance and helps target version-specific probes, but does not provide access by itself.
findings.remediation: Remove unnecessary response headers and custom platform/panel headers; use generic error pages.

findings.title: No security.txt disclosure channel
findings.impact: Researchers have no clear official route for responsibly reporting vulnerabilities.
findings.remediation: Publish an RFC 9116 security.txt with contact, expiry, languages, policy, and acknowledgement details.

positive_controls: TLS 1.0 and 1.1 were rejected; TLS 1.2 and 1.3 were accepted.
HTTP redirects to HTTPS and the certificate was valid during testing.
The session cookie uses Secure, HttpOnly, and SameSite=Lax.
Both observed POST donation forms contain CSRF tokens.
The tested CORS preflight did not return Access-Control-Allow-Origin and advertised only GET,HEAD.
.env and .git/HEAD returned 403; tested backup, log, composer, debug, and server-status paths returned 404; uploads directory listing returned 403.
not_verified_without_authorized_staging_: SQL injection, command injection, SSRF, XXE, unsafe deserialization, file-upload bypass, and remote code execution.
Authentication bypass, IDOR, role escalation, admin-panel security, MFA, password policy, and account recovery.
Payment callback validation, amount tampering, replay protection, webhook signatures, and PCI DSS scope.
Database encryption, secrets management, WAF rules, rate limiting, backups, restore testing, logs, and incident response.
Whether the identified client-side CVE paths receive attacker-controlled data in the real application.
